turns.speaker: wren
turns.text: Hi Sam, I'm Wren. It's really nice to meet you. How are you holding up today?

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: Hey Wren. Honestly, I'm pretty wiped out. Juggling a full-time schedule at the store while trying to hunt for jobs on the side is just exhausting.

turns.speaker: wren
turns.text: That is a heavy load to carry. What made you decide to start looking for customer success roles right now?

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: Well, after running the retail shop for six years, I noticed my favorite part is solving problems for clients and keeping relationships intact, rather than just stocking shelves. Customer success just feels like the right fit.

turns.speaker: wren
turns.text: Six years is a lot of customer problems solved. Is there one situation you handled that really sticks with you?

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: Oh, definitely. We had this huge crisis once where an order for an entire wedding party just vanished right before the event.

turns.speaker: wren
turns.text: That sounds terrifying for everyone involved. How did you step in?

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: The bride was in tears and shouting. I took her aside to get her calm, and then I called around our sister branches and got an exact replacement ready within two hours, so she walked away completely happy.

turns.speaker: wren
turns.text: Turning someone from panic to relief in two hours is huge. Did you know right away you wanted to use that in interviews?

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: I hoped to, yeah. I guess I was just a little worried tech interviewers wouldn't care about a retail crisis.

turns.speaker: wren
turns.text: De-escalation and fast turnarounds matter everywhere. Want to practice tightening that story into a solid behavioral answer next time?

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: Yeah, I'd really like that. Rehearsing it out loud will probably help me keep it focused.

turns.speaker: wren
turns.text: We will get it dialed in. For now, since you are so worn down from work, can you take the rest of the evening off?

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: Oh, absolutely. Dinner, couch, and straight to sleep. Thanks, Wren.
